Experiment 1: simple modules

Test generation for Arduino Uno firmware: 15 simple modules (LEDs, buttons, motors) × 3 models × RAG off/on, 1 run per cell, offline avr8js simulator

90runs: 15 modules × 6 conditions
0infrastructure errors
90 / 90tests compiled (89 on the first attempt)
69 / 90tests passed on the original module
0.83mean mutation score (572 of 690 mutants killed)
$2.10LLM cost of the whole experiment

Statistics are in analysis/REPORT.md: no RAG off / on comparison is significant after the Holm correction; GPT-5.6 Terra and Sonnet 5 produce a valid test significantly more often than Haiku 4.5; Terra kills more mutants than Sonnet. This page is a descriptive view of the same 90 runs.

Each cell is one run. Blue tests passed on the original (correct) module and were run against 10 mutants; yellow ones failed on the original module, so no mutants were run for them.

90 of 90 tests compiled, 89 on the first attempt. Passed on the original module: Terra 28 of 30, Sonnet 26, Haiku 15.

The experiment 1 prompt asked for 3–8 tests (band). Haiku wrote 7–12, Sonnet 6–8, Terra 5–8. The modules are small: 1.5–3.9 thousand characters of code.

Which mutants (injected bugs) each test catches. Grey columns: the test failed on the original module. 15 of 150 mutants were killed by no test.

The whole experiment cost $2.10 at API prices; Sonnet 5 accounts for 56%.
